units.text: Sometimes when comparing two directories, a file may exist in one directory but not the other. If you give ⟦0⟧ the ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧) option, or if you supply an old or new file that is named ⟦3⟧ or is empty and is dated the Epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC), ⟦4⟧ outputs a patch that adds or deletes the contents of this file. When given such a patch, ⟦5⟧ normally creates a new file or removes the old file. However, when conforming to POSIX (see ⟦6⟧⟦7⟧ and the POSIX Standard⟦8⟧), ⟦9⟧ does not remove the old file, but leaves it empty. The ⟦10⟧ (⟦11⟧) option causes ⟦12⟧ to remove output files that are empty after applying a patch, even if the patch does not appear to be one that removed the file.
units.sourceHTML: Sometimes when comparing two directories, a file may exist in one directory but not the other. If you give diff the --new-file (-N) option, or if you supply an old or new file that is named /dev/null or is empty and is dated the Epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC), diff outputs a patch that adds or deletes the contents of this file. When given such a patch, patch normally creates a new file or removes the old file. However, when conforming to POSIX (see patch and the POSIX Standard), patch does not remove the old file, but leaves it empty. The --remove-empty-files (-E) option causes patch to remove output files that are empty after applying a patch, even if the patch does not appear to be one that removed the file.

units.text: If the patch appears to create a file that already exists, ⟦0⟧ asks for confirmation before applying the patch.
units.sourceHTML: If the patch appears to create a file that already exists, patch asks for confirmation before applying the patch.
